questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: In the context of Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions, what is the major organic product when 1,3-Butadiene + Maleic anhydride reacts under the following conditions: Benzene solvent, reflux (80°C)?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Concerted [4+2] pericyclic cycloaddition of s-cis diene with dienophile yielding a cyclohexene adduct with syn stereospecificity. The correct major product is 'cis-1,2,3,6-Tetrahydrophthalic anhydride'.

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: In the context of Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions, what is the major organic product when Cyclopentadiene + Methyl acrylate reacts under the following conditions: 25°C in CH₂Cl₂?
questions.explanation: Major product rationale: Secondary orbital overlap between dienophile carbonyl π system and developing diene π system stabilizes the endo transition state. The correct major product is 'endo-Methyl bicyclo[2.2.1]hept-5-ene-2-carboxylate (Major endo product)'.

questions.topic: Kinetic vs Thermodynamic Bromination of Diene

questions.question: In the context of Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions, what is the major organic product when 1,3-Butadiene + Br₂ reacts under the following conditions: CH₂Cl₂ at 40°C?

questions.chapter_title: Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions
questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert (2E,4E)-Hexadiene into trans-3,4-Dimethylcyclobutene (Disrotatory closure) in Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions?

questions.question: Which reaction conditions / reagents are required to convert 1,5-Hexadiene into 1,5-Hexadiene (Equilibrated degenerate [3,3]-sigmatropic shift) in Conjugated Pi Systems and Pericyclic Reactions?

questions.topic: Claisen Rearrangement of Allyl Phenyl Ether

Mechanistic rationale: Thermal [3,3]-sigmatropic rearrangement yields a cyclohexadienone intermediate that rapidly tautomerizes to ortho-allylphenol.
